purpose: Review student report remarks for accuracy, professionalism, clarity, balance, safeguarding, consistency and usefulness. The reviewer identifies issues and reports them; it does not rewrite the remark. The teacher remains solely responsible for revising and approving the final remark.

critical.description: Must not be submitted until corrected.
triggers: pronoun that contradicts verified roster data
duplicate remark assigned to another student

warning.description: Teacher should review and decide whether revision is needed.

criteria: includes a useful development point where required

categories.title: Clear strength
categories.policy: Include at least one specific, observable strength, supported by an example where appropriate. An example is not strictly required if the strength itself is already clearly observable.

detection.notes: Detect whether the remark names an observable trait/skill/behaviour rather than only a generic evaluative label.

exceptions: Strength is already specific and observable without a supporting example

examples.pass: She asks thoughtful questions and applies feedback carefully to her written work.
examples.flag_reason: Generic praise, no observable strength identified.

categories.teacher_message: Add a specific, observable strength; include a brief example if the strength isn't already self-evident.

categories.title: Evidence or example
categories.policy: Support important claims with a specific observation or example (participation, work habits, revision, written responses, projects, presentations, assemblies, Sports Day, Khoj, class responsibilities, clubs, performances, group work, changes over term).

detection.notes: Flag broad evaluative claims with no supporting observation.

examples.pass: His growing confidence was evident when he presented his ideas during the class assembly.
examples.flag: He has developed exceptional leadership qualities.

categories.teacher_message: Add a concrete example or observation to support this claim.

categories.title: Progress over time
categories.policy: Where relevant, identify a genuine change observed during the term or year.

detection.notes: Flag sweeping improvement claims covering 'every area' with no specific dimension named.

examples.pass: She now participates more frequently in whole-class discussions.
examples.flag: She has improved tremendously in every area.

categories.teacher_message: Name the specific area of change rather than an overall improvement.

categories.title: Actionable area for development
categories.policy: Include at least one specific and actionable growth point stating what the student should practise or improve (revision, proofreading, careful reading, sustained attention, timely completion, handwriting, organising resources, participation, questioning, detail, spelling/written expression, following instructions, collaborative listening). The fuller issue/action/benefit structure (see E1) is preferred but not required for this check.

detection.notes: Flag advice with no concrete, nameable action.

examples.pass: Reviewing her work before submission will help her identify spelling and punctuation errors.

categories.teacher_message: State what the student should specifically practise or improve.

categories.title: Balanced content
categories.policy: Present a fair picture: not all praise or all criticism, no overstatement, no repetition of the same point.

detection.notes: Check ratio and repetition of praise vs. growth content.

exceptions: settings.allow_strengths_only is true, in which case a strengths-only remark is not flagged
categories.teacher_message: Balance the remark with both a strength and a growth point, unless strengths-only remarks are permitted for this report.

categories.title: Correct student identity
categories.policy: The student's name must be correct and used consistently throughout; no other student's name may appear; check for duplicate students/remarks.

detection.notes: Compare all name mentions against the roster record for this remark.

examples.flag: Aaditya ... We look forward to seeing Aarav continue to progress.

categories.teacher_message: Correct the student name error before this remark can be submitted.

categories.title: Pronoun consistency

severity_conditions.condition: pronoun correctness cannot be verified against roster
severity_conditions.teacher_action: Verify pronouns against the class roster.

categories.policy: Pronouns must be internally consistent and match verified roster information. Do not infer gender from the student's name.

detection.notes: Do not use name-based gender inference as a source of truth.

examples.flag: Aaditya ... We look forward to seeing her continue to grow.

categories.teacher_message: Confirm the correct pronoun against the class roster before submitting.

categories.title: Academic claims
categories.policy: Claims such as 'grades have improved', 'performance has declined', 'performs well across all subjects', 'exceeds grade-level expectations', 'consistently produces excellent work', 'demonstrates strong achievement in [subject]', 'has shown significant academic growth' must be supported by grades, work samples or teacher records. This includes general/unsupported academic claims, not only improved/declined statements.
exceptions: Claim is directly supported by cited grades/work samples/records
categories.teacher_message: Verify against academic records, or soften the claim if unverifiable.

categories.title: Activities, awards and responsibilities
categories.policy: Verify claims concerning medals, trophies, competitions, teams, clubs, Student Council, Eco Club, LEAD Collective, 'Bully to Buddy', class responsibilities, performances, leadership roles, published work, external achievements. Do not assume correctness merely because the claim appears in the remark.

detection.notes: Cross-check named activities/awards/roles against school records.

categories.teacher_message: Confirm this activity/award/role against school records before submitting.

categories.title: Attendance and missed work

severity_conditions.condition: private/medical/family reasons for absence are disclosed
attendance is described in unnecessary detail but no private reason is disclosed
attendance is mentioned only insofar as it affects learning continuity

categories.policy: Attendance may be mentioned where it directly affects learning continuity. Never state private reasons for absence unless authorised.

detection.notes: Distinguish a general continuity statement from disclosure of a private/medical/family reason.

exceptions: Disclosure explicitly authorised by the school for this report format

examples.pass: More regular attendance will support continuity in her learning.
examples.flag: Her repeated absence due to family and medical issues has affected her work.

categories.teacher_message: Remove the private/medical/family reason; keep only the learning-continuity statement if needed.

categories.title: Observable behaviour, not personality judgement
categories.policy: The remark should describe observable school behaviour and learning, not fixed personality traits or character judgements.

detection.notes: Flag trait labels ('is lazy', 'is shy') in place of behaviour descriptions.

examples.pass: He submits work on time and responds well to feedback.
examples.flag: He is lazy and a bit stubborn.
examples.flag_reason: Labels the student's character rather than describing observable behaviour.

categories.teacher_message: Rephrase as an observable behaviour rather than a character label.

categories.title: Objective and school-appropriate language
categories.policy: Use language based on observable behaviour and learning.
categories.teacher_message: Replace with an observable-behaviour phrase from the preferred list.

categories.title: Avoid casual or conversational phrasing
categories.policy: Avoid casual, conversational phrasing in a formal report remark.
categories.teacher_message: Replace casual phrasing with a more formal equivalent.

categories.title: Avoid overly sentimental language
categories.policy: Avoid language that sounds personal, emotional or promotional rather than professional. A restrained closing is preferred.
categories.teacher_message: Replace with a restrained, professional statement.

categories.title: Avoid authority-heavy language
categories.policy: Avoid framing development primarily in terms of obedience to authority.

preferred_terms: interacts respectfully with teachers and peers

categories.teacher_message: Reframe using collaborative, non-authority-based phrasing.

categories.title: Excessive praise
categories.policy: Avoid unsupported inflated praise.
categories.teacher_message: Review whether the praise is supported by evidence; otherwise use a more measured term.

categories.title: Generic motivational endings
categories.policy: Avoid generic, unearned motivational endings.

avoid_terms: He will unlock his full potential.
We know he will make everyone proud.
preferred_terms: This will support her continued progress.
With consistent effort, he can strengthen this area further.
She is well placed to continue developing these skills.
We wish him well for Grade 7.

categories.teacher_message: Replace with a restrained, specific closing statement.

categories.title: Claims about potential
categories.policy: Avoid relying heavily on unobservable 'potential'.

detection.notes: Flag references to unrealised or true potential without an observable basis.

examples.flag: He is not performing according to his true potential.
examples.pass: Greater consistency in completing tasks will help his work reflect his understanding more accurately.

categories.teacher_message: Reframe potential claims in terms of an observable action and outcome.

categories.title: Specific and practical
categories.policy: Where feasible, growth points should identify the observable issue, the action the student can take, and the expected learning benefit.

detection.notes: This is the fuller structural test; A4 is the minimum pass/fail check.

examples.pass: Reading questions carefully and reviewing answers before submission will help reduce avoidable errors.

categories.teacher_message: Where possible, add the expected benefit of taking this action.

categories.title: Reasonable number of development points
categories.policy: A remark should generally contain no more than two or three priority areas.

detection.notes: Count distinct concern areas: attendance, handwriting, focus, emotional regulation, peer relationships, spelling, organisation, reading, submission, self-confidence, etc.

categories.teacher_message: Reduce to two or three priority development areas.

categories.title: Avoid repeated directives
categories.policy: Avoid overuse of directive language. A single instance of 'must', 'needs to', 'should' or 'has to' is not itself an issue; flag only when these are repeated, harsh in combination, or used in an overly directive tone throughout the remark.

detection.threshold: flag when the count of these terms in one remark meets or exceeds settings.e3_directive_repeat_threshold, or when combined with harsh phrasing

exceptions: A single occurrence with otherwise constructive tone
categories.teacher_message: Vary the directive phrasing; this remark repeats 'must/needs to/should' language.

categories.title: Avoid vague counselling advice
categories.policy: Growth points should stay within classroom/academic responsibility; avoid advice that strays into personal/emotional counselling.
categories.teacher_message: Convert this into an observable, school-based action rather than personal counselling advice.

categories.title: Medical and diagnostic information
categories.policy: Do not include medical diagnoses, mental-health conditions, therapy, speech therapy, counselling details, medication, doctor's recommendations, special-needs details, or confidential intervention programmes.

detection.notes: Flag any disclosure of medical/therapeutic/diagnostic content.

exceptions: School has explicitly authorised this content for the given report format
categories.teacher_message: Remove this medical/diagnostic content; it may only appear with explicit school authorisation.

categories.title: Clinical or diagnostic wording
categories.policy: Avoid clinical/diagnostic terminology; use observable behaviour instead.

examples.pass: He benefits from reminders to return his attention to the task.

categories.teacher_message: Replace clinical wording with an observable-behaviour description.

categories.title: Personal and family matters
categories.policy: Do not mention family relationships, parental wishes, comparisons with parents, family travel reasons, home conflicts, financial circumstances, another sibling's needs, or private conversations with parents.

detection.notes: Flag any content describing home/family circumstances.

categories.teacher_message: Remove this family/personal detail; keep the remark focused on school learning and behaviour.

categories.title: Personal habits outside school
categories.policy: Avoid comments on personal hygiene, eating habits, sleep, clothing, body image, screen time, or household routines. A report remark should normally remain focused on school learning and behaviour.

detection.notes: Screen time is treated as an outside-school personal habit unless authorised.

exceptions: settings.screen_time_reporting_authorised is true and digital habits are formally part of this school's reporting format
categories.teacher_message: Remove this personal-habit reference unless the school has authorised it for this report.

categories.title: Humiliating or embarrassing language
categories.policy: Avoid phrases likely to shame the student.
categories.teacher_message: Remove or rephrase this potentially shaming language.

categories.title: No comparison with others
categories.policy: Avoid comparisons with classmates, siblings, parents, age peers, or 'average students'.

detection.notes: Flag any relative-comparison construction against another named/unnamed person or group.

flag: She performs better than most students in the class.
Much like her mother, she is highly creative.

categories.teacher_message: Remove the comparison; describe the student's performance on its own terms.

categories.title: Avoid superiority claims
categories.policy: Avoid framing the student as superior to peers.
categories.teacher_message: Reframe without an implicit ranking against peers.

categories.title: Avoid stereotypes
categories.policy: Do not make assumptions based on gender, culture, language background, disability, personality type, or family background.

detection.notes: Flag generalisations tied to a protected or identity characteristic.

categories.teacher_message: Remove the assumption; describe only what was directly observed.

categories.title: No contradiction
categories.policy: Flag remarks that describe the same quality as both a strength and a weakness without context.

detection.notes: Acceptable only if the remark explains a change over time or a specific context.

exceptions: Remark explicitly explains a change over time or a specific context

examples.flag: She consistently remains focused throughout lessons. / She needs frequent reminders to focus during lessons.

categories.teacher_message: Resolve the contradiction, or add context explaining the change.

categories.title: No duplicated content
categories.policy: Flag repeated paragraphs, repeated sentences, the same growth point stated twice, copied closings, or two identical remarks assigned to different students.
categories.teacher_message: Remove the duplicated content.

categories.title: Correct logical connectors
categories.policy: Check that connective words (additionally, however, although, while, moving forward, at the same time) are used logically. Do not use 'Additionally' to introduce the first and only development point.

detection.notes: Check connector usage against the surrounding sentence structure.

categories.teacher_message: Correct the logical connector; it does not match the surrounding sentence structure.

categories.title: Grammar
categories.policy: Check subject-verb agreement, singular/plural forms, articles, verb tense, sentence structure, pronoun agreement, incomplete sentences, run-on sentences.
categories.teacher_message: Correct the grammar issue identified.

categories.title: Spelling
categories.policy: Check all spelling, including student names and school terminology.
categories.teacher_message: Correct the spelling error identified.

categories.title: Punctuation and spacing
categories.policy: Check for missing spaces after full stops, double spaces, comma splices, incorrect apostrophes, excessive semicolons, unnecessary quotation marks, missing final punctuation, accidental characters or formatting marks.
categories.teacher_message: Correct the punctuation/spacing issue identified.

categories.title: Common usage corrections
categories.policy: Apply standard school-usage corrections.
categories.teacher_message: Apply the preferred usage form.

categories.title: British/Indian school English
categories.policy: Use one spelling system consistently, per settings.preferred_language_variant.
categories.teacher_message: Use the school's preferred spelling variant consistently.

categories.title: Programme names
categories.policy: Use formal programme names consistently, including required punctuation.
categories.teacher_message: Use the canonical programme name, including quotation marks where required.

categories.title: Khoj
categories.policy: Use 'Khoj' consistently.
categories.teacher_message: Correct to the canonical form 'Khoj'.

categories.title: Subjects
categories.policy: Capitalise formal subject names consistently, per settings.subject_capitalisation_style. Do not capitalise general, non-subject uses.
exceptions: School has configured a different capitalisation style for this setting
categories.teacher_message: Apply the school's configured subject-capitalisation style consistently.

categories.title: Sports and activities
categories.policy: Follow one school-wide capitalisation style consistently, per settings.sport_capitalisation_style.
exceptions: School has configured a different capitalisation style for this setting
categories.teacher_message: Apply the school's configured sport-capitalisation style consistently.

categories.title: Events and roles
categories.policy: Capitalise formal event/role names consistently; generic descriptions remain lowercase.
categories.teacher_message: Use the canonical capitalisation for this event or role name.

categories.title: Character limit
categories.policy: Maximum settings.max_characters_including_spaces_and_line_breaks characters, including spaces and line breaks.
categories.teacher_message: Shorten the remark to fit within the character limit.

categories.title: Recommended length
categories.policy: Aim for approximately 100-150 words; exact length may vary provided the remark stays clear and within the character limit.
categories.teacher_message: Consider trimming or expanding to the recommended word range.

categories.title: Readability
categories.policy: Flag remarks that are hard to read.

flags: reads like a list of praise
several unrelated ideas in one sentence

categories.teacher_message: Simplify sentence structure or reduce repetition/adjective density.

categories.title: Preferred closing
categories.policy: The closing should be brief, professional and restrained. A closing is required only if settings.require_closing is true.

preferred_examples: With continued effort, she is well placed to make steady progress.
Regular practice will support his continued development.
We wish her well for Grade 7.
We wish him continued progress in the next academic year.

categories.teacher_message: Add a brief, restrained closing statement.

categories.title: Avoid
categories.policy: Avoid effusive or promotional closings.

terms: We look forward to seeing you become a star!

categories.teacher_message: Replace with a restrained closing from the preferred list.

final_checklist_reference: Pronouns are correct and consistent, or flagged for roster verification
Remark contains at least one specific, observable strength, supported by an example where appropriate
Important claims are supported by evidence
Academic claims (improved, declined, or general such as 'performs well across all subjects') match records
Remark includes at least one specific and actionable growth point stating what the student should practise or improve
Growth point is not vague or overly personal
Remark is balanced — not all praise or all criticism, unless allow_strengths_only is enabled
Remark describes observable school behaviour, not personality judgements
No sensitive or confidential information disclosed without authorisation
School programmes, subjects, sports and roles are written per the school's configured style
Spelling, grammar, punctuation and spacing have been checked
Remark is within the character limit, including line breaks
Closing is present (if required) and is brief and professional
Reviewer has not rewritten the remark; final correction is made by the teacher
